title: Current Non-Sustainable Farming Practices Explained
reason: The video describes various unsustainable agricultural practices and the changes needed for sustainable farming.

tasks.task: Discuss historical agricultural practices and their impact on the environment.

subtasks.text: Observe the picture of native prairie land that shows how it was farmed before modern techniques.
Note how plowing open fields leads to soil erosion during winter.
Highlight the changes made to protect the environment, such as the introduction of conservation practices starting in the late 1960s.

tasks.task: Explain the current tillage practices in modern agriculture and their environmental implications.

subtasks.text: Point out the use of cultivation to control weeds and its limitations.
Describe the process and equipment used in disking.
Explain how minimum till and no till practices have replaced traditional plowing methods.

tasks.task: Discuss synthetic fertilizers and their impact on soil and water quality.

subtasks.text: Observe the use of anhydrous ammonia as a synthetic fertilizer on cornfields.
Highlight the long-term negative effects of synthetic fertilizers on soil vitality.
Describe how synthetic fertilizers can lead to nutrient runoff into water bodies.

tasks.task: Explore the evolution of pest and weed control practices in agriculture.

subtasks.text: Observe the use of selective herbicides and why they are beneficial.
Describe the emergence of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) in agriculture.
Highlight the potential drawbacks and concerns with GMOs.

tasks.task: Examine the shift from small family farms to large corporate farming and its implications.

subtasks.text: Note the trend of family farms being sold and replaced by larger corporate farms.
Observe the use of large feedlots for raising cattle and the environmental issues.
